questions.stem: Why do plant roots grow downwards (positive gravitropism)?

options.text: Because auxin accumulates on the lower side of the root, inhibiting growth there and causing the root to bend downwards
Because roots are heavier than shoots
Because roots need light to grow
Because gravity pulls water down and roots follow it

questions.explanation: Gravity causes auxin to accumulate on the lower side of a horizontal root. Since high auxin concentration inhibits root cell elongation, the upper side grows faster, bending the root downwards.
